chapter: Fats Waller, Zululand and the ideal band
title: Slam Stewart
summary: He praises Slam Stewart as a virtuoso and tells of arco and three-part harmony.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Who would you have on bass?
bring to dig up did it? (LAUGHTER).
No, it didn't. Slam Stewart is really a virtuoso. That guy he is the bass player in my opinion. Everything, he hums along with his solos you know.
Oh, I remember that (HUMS) you get, yes.
Yes, but he's in tune. His intuition is absolutely perfect.
And he really uses the voice as an instrument along with his bass.

That is correct. That is correct. He worked with me up in Syracuse a few months ago. He was with my quartet. And I'd sing a number like 'Basin Street Blues' and he would, on the last note I'd hold a note out. He'd bow one bass. arco we call it, bow, we'd bow one note, sing another note and I'd sing another note. We had three-part harmony there. But I didn't ask him to do it. He just did it. You see, this is what I'm talking about. This shows his musicianship and his empathy.
What is that word you just used I don't know that technical term?
Bow, that means bowing, that's all. But Slam Stewart......
